description:
FILED s463av while writing §0.2f.  This is a QUESTION with its discriminating
measurement half taken, not a diagnosis — the half that is taken rules out the
two most recent rounds, and the half that is left needs a machine this session
could not get.

THE OBSERVATION.  Comparing PCL ABSOLUTE seconds (the §0.2a rule) against
§0.2d's numbers, which were taken on a quiet box at s458ak:

    row          §0.2d      s463av (best of 6 runs)   delta
    intloop+=    0.0174     0.0209                    +20 %
    cfor         0.0261     0.0302                    +16 %
    intloop=     0.0185     0.0182                     -2 %   <- unchanged
    gcdrec       0.0942     0.0949                     +1 %
    fib(27)x     0.4196     0.4315                     +3 %

perl's own column is flat across the same span (§0.2b `intloop+=` perl
0.0647 s, s463av 0.0667 s), which is what makes it worth asking: under the
§0.2a rule, "PCL up, perl flat" is the signature of a real PCL-side move, and
it is exactly how `symref`'s +34 % was found and then bisected to #525/#685.

THE SHAPE LOOKED LIKE A HYPOTHESIS.  The two rows that moved both contain a
compound assignment or a `++` (`$s += $_`; `for (my $i=0; $i<$n; $i++)`), and
the one that did not move is the plain `$s = $s + $_`.  Round 19's #934 had
just reworked exactly that path (`%define-compound-pair` gained a supplied-p,
`$x++` routes to `perl-increment`).

THE MEASUREMENT KILLS IT.  Five interleaved best-of-5 A/B runs of the s463av
runtime (A) against ROUND 18's runtime (`4c354bc`, B) — same emission, one
transpile, two cores:

    cfor       B/A +9.3 %   (+9.9 +6.0 +7.3 +9.3 +20.7)   all five positive
    intloop+=  B/A +2.8 %   (-10.3 +3.6 +6.8 +2.8 -6.9)   sign-mixed
    intloop=   B/A +3.2 %   (+10.9 -9.0 +5.4 +3.2 -0.5)   sign-mixed
    gcdrec     B/A +1.5 %   sign-mixed

Round 18 is SLOWER, consistently so on `cfor`.  So rounds 18 and 19 did not
cause the gap; whatever it is, it is older than `4c354bc` — or it is not real
at all and §0.2d's "quiet box" was quieter than anything available in s463av
(1-minute load ran 1.3 to 7.7 all session, with a sibling agent and the
reviewer live).

WHAT TO DO, ON A QUIET BOX, IN ABOUT TEN MINUTES:

 1. `perl tools/bench-exec.pl intloop cfor` twice at 1-min load < 0.3.  If
    `intloop+=` comes in at ~0.0174 and `cfor` at ~0.0261, THIS TASK IS CLOSED
    as machine state and §0.2f's note should say so.
 2. If they do not, bisect exactly as §0.2a did for `symref` — the tool now
    makes it one command per commit instead of a worktree per commit:

        git show <sha>:cl/pcl-runtime.lisp > /tmp/rt-<sha>.lisp
        BENCH_RT_B=/tmp/rt-<sha>.lisp perl tools/bench-exec.pl intloop cfor

    (`BENCH_RT_B` stages the file into cl/ for the core build, so
    *pcl-runtime-directory* resolves and the pack rows still run.)  Candidate
    span: everything between s458ak and `4c354bc`, i.e. rounds 15 to 18.  Note
    that this only moves the RUNTIME; if the bisect comes up empty the cause is
    an EMISSION change and needs a worktree per commit after all.

NOT URGENT: both rows beat perl by 3x either way.  It matters because an
unexplained 20 % on the project's fastest shapes is exactly the kind of drift
§0.2a was written to catch, and because leaving it unlabelled means the next
re-tabulation compares against a number nobody trusts.

ADDENDUM s463av, the quietest sample the session got (1-min load 1.24, one
best-of-5 run on the merged tree):

    intloop=   0.0177   <- BELOW its §0.2d record of 0.0185
    intloop+=  0.0213   <- still above 0.0174   (+22 %)
    cfor       0.0291   <- still above 0.0261   (+11 %)

So the effect does NOT dissolve as the box quietens: `intloop=` reaches and
passes its record at load 1.24 while the other two do not.  That makes plain
machine state a weaker explanation than it looked, and step 1 of the recipe
above (two runs at load < 0.3) correspondingly more worth doing.

STEP 1 TAKEN, s464ax (2026-09-02) â AND IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE TASK.

The box was genuinely quiet: 1-minute load **0.12 / 0.15 / 0.36** across three
consecutive `perl tools/bench-exec.pl intloop cfor` runs (BENCH_K=5, the whole
thing takes 5.5 s), no sibling agent running, nothing else on 16 cores.

    run          intloop+=   intloop=   cfor
    1            0.0203      0.0190     0.0293
    2            0.0223      0.0188     0.0285
    3            0.0212      0.0193     0.0293
    best         0.0203      0.0188     0.0285
    Â§0.2d record 0.0174      0.0185     0.0261
    delta        +17 %       +2 %       +9 %

perl's own column was flat and matches the record (0.0663-0.0673 for
`intloop+=`, 0.0994-0.1070 for `cfor`).

So the recipe's step-1 verdict is **NOT machine state**: `intloop=` reaches
its record on this box while the other two do not, exactly as the s463av
addendum at load 1.24 already suggested.  The two rows that moved are the ones
containing a compound assignment or a `++`; the one that did not is the plain
`$s = $s + $_`.

WHAT IS LEFT is step 2 â the `BENCH_RT_B` bisect over rounds **15 to 18**
(s463av's own five-run A/B already showed round 18's runtime, `4c354bc`, is
SLOWER on `cfor` by +9.3 % with all five samples positive, so the cause is
older than that or is an EMISSION change, which needs a worktree per commit).
Note for whoever takes it: the whole measurement is 5.5 s per commit, so the
bisect is minutes, not a session â the expensive part is only building each
core.


=== DONE (s473r, 2026-09-07) â the commit, the cause, and the size ===

STEP 2 TAKEN.  The gap is REAL, its commit is `bfa170d9`, and the cost is
INTENDED â a correctness fix that must dispatch.  Closed on that ground, with
the residue filed as #1516.

1. THE RECORD REPRODUCES, so machine state is dead by REPRODUCTION and not
   only by inference.  A `git archive f49a34df` extraction (s458ak, the tree
   Â§0.2d was measured on) benched on THIS box in a quiet window (1-min load
   1.5, perl flat at 0.065-0.067 / 0.105-0.106 across both trees, three
   interleaved rounds, BENCH_K=7):

       row         s458ak tree   today`s tree   today/old   Â§0.2d record
       intloop+=      0.0175        0.0206       +17.7 %       0.0174
       intloop=       0.0175        0.0179        +2.3 %       0.0185
       cfor           0.0253        0.0266        +5.1 %       0.0261

   The old tree hits Â§0.2d`s numbers to the fourth decimal.  Nothing about
   the machine changed; the code did.

2. THE `BENCH_RT_B` RECIPE IN THIS TASK CANNOT SEE IT, and that is worth
   recording: today`s emission does not run on the s458ak runtime at all
   (`BROKEN: pclB exit 1` on every row), so the one-command-per-commit form
   only works across a few generations.  A `git archive` extraction per
   commit does work and is what was used.

3. THE EMISSION IS BYTE-IDENTICAL, which localises it without any timing.
   `my $s=0; for (1..$n) { $s += $_ }` lowers to
   `(p-foreach-range-raw ($_ 1 $n) (p-incf-raw $s $_))` on BOTH trees (only
   the surrounding `let` -> `p-let` and the `\n` -> `p-esc` differ).  So the
   whole move is in the RUNTIME`s p-incf-raw.

4. THE COMMIT.  `git log -S %compound-arith-form -- cl/pcl-runtime.lisp`
   answers `bfa170d9` (s461ar, ROUND 18, "#900 + #911 â `++` keeps the
   OBJECT").  p-incf-raw`s body went from

       `(+ (to-number ,cur) (to-number ,delta))

   to `%compound-arith-form`, i.e. `(if (and *p-any-overload-registered*
   BLESSED) slow plain)` â perl`s `+=`/`++` overload dispatch, which PCL had
   been skipping (a class`s `+` handler was numified and the object lost).

5. THE SIZE, measured load-robustly (ab-lisp.pl: two .lisp files, ONE core,
   interleaved, best-of-7, N = 5e6, byte-identical but for one form):

       (p-incf-raw $s $_)            0.0246 s
       (p-incf-raw $s $_ :numeric)   0.0209 s      -15.1 %

   15.1 % of the row against the 17.7 % observed â and the remaining 2.6 %,
   like cfor`s 5.1 % and intloop=`s 2.3 %, is inside the CORE-LAYOUT band:
   a runtime built from bfa11c72 plus two NEVER-CALLED functions of the same
   size moves cfor -3.6 % and intloop+= -5.6 % (s473r`s #1514 control).  A
   few % on the tightest rows will never bisect to a cause.

6. WHY IT IS NOT REVERTED.  DECIDED Â§s470 already ruled it: "the #1153
   slowdown is RULED â the correctness fix stays; the guard-free path is a
   PERF lever, not a revert."  The lever EXISTS: `numeric-slot` (#1183) drops
   the guard when the emitter proves the slot numeric.  It does not license
   `$s += $_`, because `$_` is not a compile-time number literal â and that
   is the residue, filed as **#1516** with this 15.1 % beside it.

Â§0.2f should now say: the drift is #900`s overload dispatch, measured at
15.1 % of intloop+=, owned by #1516; the rest is core layout.
subject: Perf, UNSETTLED: `intloop+=` and `cfor` read ~16-20 % above their §0.2d quiet-box absolutes while `intloop=` matches exactly — rounds 18/19 RULED OUT by A/B; needs ten minutes on a quiet box
